functions.name: addAzureKubernetesEnvironment
functions.description: Adds an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) environment to the distributed application. This provisions an AKS cluster and configures it as a Kubernetes compute environment.
functions.remarks:
This method internally creates a Kubernetes environment for Helm-based deployment
and provisions an AKS cluster via Azure Bicep. It combines the functionality of
`AddKubernetesEnvironment` with Azure-specific provisioning.
The cluster uses the Standard control-plane tier by default, which includes an uptime SLA
and a cluster-management charge. Use `ConfigureInfrastructure` to select a different tier.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the AKS environment resource.

functions.name: addCertManager
functions.description: Installs cert-manager into an AKS environment

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The Aspire resource name for the cert-manager installation.

parameters.name: chartVersion
parameters.description: The cert-manager Helm chart version to install. Defaults to a pinned version validated against this Aspire build.

functions.name: addGateway
functions.description: Adds a Kubernetes Gateway API Gateway resource to the application model, associated with the inner Kubernetes environment of the specified AKS environment.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the gateway resource.

functions.name: addHelmChart
functions.description: Adds an external Helm chart to be installed in the AKS environment's inner Kubernetes environment. The chart is installed via `helm upgrade --install` as a pipeline step after the main application Helm chart is deployed.
functions.remarks:
This method delegates to the inner `KubernetesEnvironmentResource` of the AKS
environment, so the returned `KubernetesHelmChartResource` can be configured
with the same `WithHelmValue`,
`WithNamespace`,
`WithReleaseName`, and
`WithDestroy` extensions used with
non-AKS Kubernetes environments.
External Helm charts are not uninstalled by `aspire destroy` by default,
because they may be shared with workloads outside the Aspire app. Opt in by chaining
`WithDestroy`.
functions.returns: A resource builder for the Helm chart resource.
functions.signature: addHelmChart(name: string, chartReference: string, chartVersion: string): KubernetesHelmChartResource

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the Helm chart resource.

parameters.name: chartReference
parameters.description: The Helm chart reference. Can be an OCI registry URL (e.g., `oci://quay.io/jetstack/charts/cert-manager`) or a chart name from an added repository.

parameters.name: chartVersion
parameters.description: The chart version to install.

functions.name: addIngress
functions.description: Adds a Kubernetes Ingress resource to the application model, associated with the inner Kubernetes environment of the specified AKS environment. The ingress generates a `networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress` resource in the Helm chart output at publish time.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the ingress resource.

functions.name: addLoadBalancer
functions.description: Adds an Azure Application Gateway for Containers (AGC) `ApplicationLoadBalancer` to this AKS environment, bound to the supplied delegated subnet. Returns a resource builder that can be passed to `gateway.WithLoadBalancer(lb)` / `ingress.WithLoadBalancer(lb)` to route traffic through this load balancer.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the load balancer resource. Used to derive the in-cluster `ApplicationLoadBalancer` name (`alb-{name}`) referenced by gateway/ingress annotations.

parameters.name: subnet
parameters.description: A subnet that will be associated with the AGC ALB. The subnet is automatically delegated to `Microsoft.ServiceNetworking/trafficControllers`; this is required by AGC and is idempotent across multiple `AddLoadBalancer` calls against the same subnet.

functions.name: addNodePool
functions.description: Adds a node pool to the AKS cluster using a configuration callback.
functions.remarks:
The callback receives the node pool configuration with default VM size and node counts.
Configuration remains mutable and is validated during infrastructure generation.
Omitting the OS SKU leaves AKS to choose its default.
The returned resource can be used to schedule workloads on this pool.
functions.returns: The resource builder for the new node pool.
functions.signature: addNodePool(name: string, configure: (obj: AksNodePoolConfig) => Promise<void>): AksNodePoolResource

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the node pool.

parameters.name: configure
parameters.description: A callback to configure VM size, autoscaling, and OS SKU.

functions.name: addPersistentVolume
functions.description: Adds a Kubernetes PersistentVolumeClaim resource to an AKS environment

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the persistent volume resource.

functions.name: withContainerRegistry
functions.description: Configures the AKS environment to use a specific Azure Container Registry for image storage. When set, this replaces the auto-created default container registry.
functions.remarks:
If not called, a default Azure Container Registry is automatically created.
The registry endpoint is flowed to the inner Kubernetes environment so that
Helm deployments can push and pull images.

parameters.name: registry
parameters.description: The Azure Container Registry resource builder.

functions.name: withLoadBalancer
functions.description: Routes a Kubernetes Gateway through an AGC ApplicationLoadBalancer
functions.remarks:
Writes the AGC routing annotations (`alb.networking.azure.io/alb-name` and
`alb.networking.azure.io/alb-namespace`) onto the rendered Gateway and defaults
the GatewayClass to `azure-alb-external` when one has not already been set via
`WithGatewayClass(...)`.

parameters.name: loadBalancer
parameters.description: The AGC load balancer to route through.

functions.name: withLoadBalancer
functions.description: Routes a Kubernetes Ingress through an AGC ApplicationLoadBalancer
functions.remarks:
Writes the AGC routing annotations (`alb.networking.azure.io/alb-name` and
`alb.networking.azure.io/alb-namespace`) onto the rendered Ingress and defaults
the IngressClass to `azure-alb-external` when one has not already been set via
`WithIngressClass(...)`.

parameters.name: loadBalancer
parameters.description: The AGC load balancer to route through.

functions.name: withSubnet
functions.description: Configures the AKS cluster to use a VNet subnet

parameters.name: subnet
parameters.description: The subnet to use for AKS node pools.

functions.name: withSubnet
functions.description: Configures an AKS node pool to use a specific VNet subnet

parameters.name: subnet
parameters.description: The subnet to use for this node pool.

functions.name: withSystemNodePool
functions.description: Replaces the system node pool using a configuration callback.
functions.remarks:
Each call replaces the previous system pool configuration, starting with default VM size and node counts.
Configuration remains mutable and is validated during infrastructure generation.
Omitting the OS SKU leaves AKS to choose its default.
functions.returns: The AKS environment resource builder for chaining.

parameters.name: configure
parameters.description: A callback to configure VM size, autoscaling, and OS SKU.

functions.name: withWorkloadIdentity
functions.description: Enables or disables workload identity on the AKS environment, allowing pods to authenticate to Azure services using federated credentials.
functions.remarks:
This ensures the AKS cluster is configured with OIDC issuer and workload identity enabled.
Workload identity is automatically wired when compute resources have an `AppIdentityAnnotation`,
which is added by `WithAzureUserAssignedIdentity` or auto-created by `AzureResourcePreparer`.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: `true` to enable workload identity (the default); `false` to disable it.

dtoTypes.name: AksNodePoolConfig
dtoTypes.description: Configuration for an AKS node pool.
dtoTypes.remarks:
Configuration remains mutable so extensions can compose changes before infrastructure generation.
The final values are validated when generating the AKS agent pool profile.
The node pool name and mode are fixed at construction to preserve pool identity.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: Gets the name of the node pool.

fields.name: Mode
fields.description: Gets the mode of the node pool.

fields.name: VmSize
fields.description: Gets or sets the VM size for nodes in the pool.

fields.name: MinCount
fields.description: Gets or sets the minimum node count for autoscaling. System pools require at least 1; user pools can scale to 0.

fields.name: MaxCount
fields.description: Gets or sets the maximum node count for autoscaling. Must be at least the minimum node count.

fields.name: OsSku
fields.description: Gets or sets the Linux OS SKU, such as `AzureLinux` or `Ubuntu`. A `null` value leaves the SKU unspecified so AKS chooses its default.

enumTypes.name: AksNodePoolMode
enumTypes.description: Specifies the mode of an AKS node pool.
